description: Dependency automation for the perfume store (owner decision: Renovate, not Dependabot).
Coverage: pip (backend/requirements.in + the hash-pinned backend/requirements.lock), npm (frontend/package.json + package-lock.json) and GitHub Actions (every workflow under .github/workflows/).

Cadence: one grouped PR per ecosystem, weekly (Monday before 06:00 UTC). MAJOR updates are never grouped and never automerged: they open one PR per dependency so a breaking migration is reviewed on its own.
No automerge anywhere: every PR here lands only after CI is green and a human merges it (the release engineer promotes; Renovate never touches master or feat/add-frontend).
Security advisories are NOT subject to the weekly window (an open CVE should not wait for Monday).
They are still not automerged: pip-audit / npm audit --audit-level=high gate the PR like any other.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Weekly lockfile refresh, so the grouped PRs never sit on a stale resolution.

description: Override the default fileMatch (which only sees requirements.txt) so the pip manager tracks the two files that actually decide the pins: requirements.in (the human-authored intent) and requirements.lock (the hash-pinned resolution CI installs).

requirements.lock is a pip-compile output: a version bump here also needs its --hash lines regenerated (pip verifies every hash, so a half-updated lock fails the install step). The rule below labels those PRs so that step is never forgotten.

packageRules.description: GitHub Actions: one grouped weekly PR per major line, digests kept pinned (SPEC-22-11). A mutable tag is a remote-controlled pointer, so Renovate rewrites the digest and keeps the tag in a trailing comment.
Backend Python: minor/patch grouped into one weekly PR (requirements.in + requirements.lock).
Frontend npm: minor/patch grouped into one weekly PR; package-lock.json rides along in the same PR (npm manager default).
A bump of the hash-pinned lock alone: the --hash lines must be regenerated by the repo's compile step before CI can install it.

MAJOR updates: never grouped (separateMultipleMajor keeps one PR per dependency), never automerged, labelled so they are triaged as migrations rather than chores. This rule is last so it also removes majors from the ecosystem groups above.
